ev: لا خلاف في كسر الهاء منه
items.lemma: كل هاء ضمير جمع أو تثنية

desc: ضم كل هاء ضمير جمع أو تثنية وقعت بعد ياو ساكنة
زاد رويس فضم ما سقطت منه الياء

items.note: Yaʿqūb agrees with Ḥamza on the three words and adds the ḍamm of the hāʾ of a dual or plural pronoun after a silent yāʾ. Ruways adds the ḍamm where the yāʾ has dropped, except in Al-Anfāl 'wa man yuwallihim', where there is no difference. The book says the rest read the kasra everywhere. Ḥamza's three words are entered under عليهم on the Sura 1 page, so 'the rest' is not computed here.

ev: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وقالون بخلاف عنه
items.note: The mīm of the plural before and after a hamza. The author reports reading the sukūn for Qālūn to Abū al-Ḥasan and the ṣila to Abū al-Fatḥ.

ev: حمزة والكسائي وخلف يضمون الهاء والميم

forms.desc: يضمون الهاء والميم إذا كان قبل الهاء كسرة أو ياء ساكنة وأتى بعد الميم ألف وصل
يكسر الهاء والميم في ذلك كله في حال الوصل

items.note: In connected reading. When they stop on the mīm they read the kasra on the hāʾ and a sukūn on the mīm, and the book says all agree that the mīm is silent on stopping. The author adds that Yaʿqūb agrees with Abū ʿAmr where no silent yāʾ precedes the hāʾ.

ev: وحمزة على أصله في الكلم الثلاث

forms.desc: يضم الهاء منهن على كل حال

items.note: The three words are عليهم, إليهم and لديهم, entered under عليهم on the Sura 1 page.

skipped.why: the Fatiha statements (malik, al-sirat, alayhim) are entered in the Sura 1 display from the same book and pages; the pilot cites this passage there
the heading and introduction of the chapter on Abu Amr's major idghām: it covers the idghām of moving letters that are alike or near in the same word or across two words
